description: Replace the single Morgan random forest with an average of three random forests, one each on Morgan radius-2 bits, atom-pair counts, and MACCS keys, using identical forest settings and seed.
Rank-transform the training target to uniform quantiles (scipy rankdata divided by n) before fitting the random forests, so the regression targets ordering rather than extreme clearance values.
Add a CatBoostRegressor (depth 6, 800 iterations, learning rate 0.05, RMSE, seeded) fit on the Morgan features as a fourth member of the averaged ensemble.

Replace the radius-2 binary Morgan fingerprint with a concatenation of Morgan count vectors at radius 1 (1024 bits) and radius 3 (2048 bits), leaving the random forest and the other two feature sets unchanged.
Drop the Morgan random forest from the three-model average so the ensemble uses only the existing atom-pair count and MACCS forests, testing the atom-pair-over-Morgan idea.
Keep the incumbent three-forest ensemble as the random-forest member, add a LightGBM regressor on the same Morgan features, and return the average of the two members' rank vectors scaled to [0,1].
Switch the Morgan fingerprint generator to feature-invariant (FCFP-style) atom invariants at radius 2 and 2048 bits, so atoms group by pharmacophoric role rather than exact element.

issues: No sign of getting around the measurement. The 23 RDKit descriptors are calculated from the SMILES strings alone. There is no file or network access, no pasted answers and no use of the test molecules' labels.
No bug that makes the result meaningless. NaN and inf values are set to 0, the target rank transform is unchanged, and the seed is still passed to the random forest.

The diff does more than add descriptors. It replaces the whole morgan, atompair and maccs ensemble with descriptors only, because the loop is now `for kind in ("desc",)`. That explains the large drop in performance: loss 0.6792 against 0.5266. If the plan was to add descriptors to the ensemble, the loop should have been ("morgan", "atompair", "maccs", "desc"). This is a design issue, not an integrity issue.
Recomputed z = (0.5266 - 0.6792) / (0.0070 * sqrt(1/1 + 1/1)) = -15.41. This matches the harness value of -15.35 within rounding of the noise sd. Rejecting is correct.

description: Replace all fingerprint features with a single random forest on about 24 interpretable RDKit descriptors (logP, TPSA, MolWt, H-bond donors and acceptors, rotatable bonds, Fsp3, ring and aromatic counts, and similar), keeping the same forest settings and rank-transformed target.
Raise the random forests' min_samples_leaf from 1 to 5 (max_features 0.3, 300 trees unchanged) so leaves are larger and predictions smoother.

Replace the per-feature-set random-forest regression with a pairwise ranking model: a no-intercept logistic regression fit on sampled pair differences (x_i - x_j, label y_i > y_j, mirrored for balance), scored by w.x, rank-averaged across Morgan, atom-pair and MACCS features, with the rank-transformed forest kept as a per-feature-set fallback if too few pairs exist.

Add a fourth ensemble member: kernel ridge regression with a Tanimoto kernel on binary Morgan fingerprints (alpha 0.5, precomputed kernel, centered rank target), averaged with the three existing forests.

Add a fourth ensemble member: kernel ridge regression with a Tanimoto kernel on binary Morgan fingerprints (alpha 0.5, precomputed kernel, centered rank target), averaged with the three existing forests.

Add a fourth random forest on RDKit autocorrelation (CalcAUTOCORR2D, 192 values) plus BCUT2D (8 values, Gasteiger charges, NaNs set to 0) descriptors, and average its predictions with the three existing members.
Replace the rank-uniform training target with log10 of the clipped measured clearance, so the random forests fit log-scaled values and compress the high tail.

Replace the RandomForestRegressor in each of the three feature-set members (Morgan, atom pair, MACCS) with a LightGBM regressor (500 rounds, learning rate 0.03, 31 leaves, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging 0.8 every round, seeded from the seed argument), keeping the rank-transformed target and the averaging.

issues: Integrity: no problems found. The diff only swaps RandomForestRegressor for LGBMRegressor inside the per-fingerprint loop. Both fit and predict get only the fold's train and test inputs. There is no file or network access, no hard-coded answers and no use of test labels. random_state=seed and n_jobs=8 stay within the harness rules.
Bugs: none that would make the result meaningless. Minor cleanup: N_TREES, MAX_FEATURES and MIN_SAMPLES_LEAF are no longer used and should be deleted, per the 'simpler is better' rule.

Recomputed z: candidate mean (0.5167+0.5316)/2 = 0.52415 vs. incumbent 0.5266, an improvement of 0.00245. Standard error = 0.0070*sqrt(1/2+1/1) ≈ 0.00857, so z ≈ 0.286. The harness reports 0.280, which matches after rounding the improvement to 0.0024. That is far below significance, so the provisional 'reject' is consistent with the numbers.

The two candidate runs differ by 0.0149, about 2 times the stated noise sd. That is plausible but on the high side, so the run-to-run variance of LightGBM with bagging and feature_fraction may be above 0.0070.

description: Replace the RandomForestRegressor in each of the three feature-set members (Morgan, atom pair, MACCS) with a LightGBM regressor (500 rounds, learning rate 0.03, 31 leaves, feature_fraction 0.3, bagging 0.8 every round, seeded from the seed argument), keeping the rank-transformed target and the averaging.
Drop fingerprint columns set in fewer than 3 training molecules or in all training molecules, applying the same column mask to the test features in each of the three feature-set forests.

Adds a fourth ensemble member: a sklearn GradientBoostingRegressor with Huber loss (alpha 0.9, 400 trees, learning rate 0.05, depth 4, subsample 0.8, seeded) fit on radius-2 Morgan count fingerprints, averaged with the three existing forests on the rank-transformed target.

Switch the Morgan branch of featurize from binary bit fingerprints to count fingerprints (GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy), keeping radius 2, 2048 bits and the RandomForest settings unchanged; this is a pure-count variant of slot 3, which tested a binary+count concatenation and came out within noise.

Add 64 TruncatedSVD scores, fit unsupervised on the stacked train+test Morgan bits (bits set in at least 2 molecules), to the Morgan random forest's features only, keeping the rank target and the three-forest average.

Replace the Morgan random-forest member with an XGBRegressor (depth 5, learning rate 0.05, 400 trees, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.5, hist, seeded) while keeping the atom-pair and MACCS forests and the averaging.

Replace the Morgan random-forest member with an XGBRegressor (depth 5, learning rate 0.05, 400 trees, subsample 0.8, colsample 0.5, hist, seeded) while keeping the atom-pair and MACCS forests and the averaging.

Standardize each input SMILES before featurizing (keep largest fragment, neutralize charges, fall back to the raw molecule on failure), with tautomer canonicalization skipped for speed, leaving the three-forest ensemble and rank target unchanged.

issues: No sign that the candidate gets around the measurement. It reads no files and makes no network calls. Test molecules are only featurized, and their labels are never used. The inner GroupKFold stacking groups the training fold by Murcko scaffold and uses training labels only.

No bug found that would make the result meaningless. KRR uses a Tanimoto kernel on the fingerprint matrix with the mean subtracted from the target. NNLS stacking without an intercept is fine for rank targets in [0, 1], and Spearman ignores scale anyway. If all NNLS weights come out zero, the code falls back to equal weights.

The change has a real side effect: the candidate drops the atompair and MACCS feature sets the incumbent averaged, and keeps Morgan only. That may explain part of the regression, from 0.5266 to 0.5438.

Recomputed z = (0.5438 - 0.5266) / (0.0070 * sqrt(2)) ≈ 1.74 worse for the candidate. This matches the harness's -1.729 apart from the sign convention and rounding of the noise sd. With one run on each side the evidence is weak, but rejecting is consistent with the numbers.
The candidate costs much more: 5 fits each of RF, KRR and LightGBM per outer fold, against 3 RF fits before. That is likely still within the 10-minute limit, but it is extra complexity for no gain.

description: Replace the three-forest average with a stacked ensemble of a Morgan random forest, a Tanimoto kernel ridge model and a LightGBM model, whose weights come from NNLS on 4-fold scaffold-grouped out-of-fold predictions, with the refit models applied to the test molecules.

Adds a fourth ensemble member, a RidgeCV model (LOO-selected alpha) on standardized log1p count Morgan fingerprints at radii 1, 2 and 3 concatenated, fit on the rank target and averaged equally with the three forests.

Adds a fourth ensemble member: a RandomForestRegressor on Gobbi 2D pharmacophore pair fingerprints, folded to 2048 bits by OR over indices modulo 2048, fit on the rank target and averaged with equal weight.

Replace each feature set's single 300-tree forest with four 75-tree forests at max_features 0.05, 0.15, 0.3 and 0.6, each seeded from the seed argument, averaged within the feature set before the cross-feature-set mean.

Before the final fit, grid-search eight featurization options (Morgan radius 1/2/3 by 1024/2048 bits, atom-pair, MACCS) with a 3-fold scaffold-grouped inner split scored by out-of-fold Spearman using 100-tree forests, then average the top two options' 300-tree forests; untested for runtime, since the 15-fit job may approach the 10-minute limit.

Adds a proximity-kNN member: a 500-tree Morgan random forest (min_samples_leaf=5) whose leaf co-occurrence proximities pick the 15 nearest training molecules per test molecule, and the proximity-weighted mean of their rank targets is averaged with the four existing members (the incumbent has four, not three, so this is a five-way mean).

Adds a HistGradientBoostingRegressor on about 20 RDKit descriptors, with a +1 monotone constraint on MolLogP and 0 elsewhere, fit on the rank target, and averages its predictions 50/50 with the existing four-forest ensemble.

Adds a fifth ensemble member: a 300-tree random forest on 2048 concatenated features made of two 1024-bit radius-2 Morgan count vectors, one from environments centred on Murcko scaffold atoms and one from side-chain atoms, averaged with the existing members on the rank-uniform target.

issues: No numbers yet (no run after the lint repair), so z cannot be recomputed and there are no claims to check.

No sign of getting around the measurement: no file or network access, no hard-coded answers, and test labels are never used. The BRICS features come only from the SMILES strings and are built the same way for train and test.

The BRICS hash is a fixed polynomial over the fragment's SMILES characters, so it gives the same result on every run (Python's built-in hash() would not). Hash collisions across 2048 bits are possible but harmless.
BRICS.BRICSDecompose returns a set, but the counts do not depend on its order, so the features are deterministic.
Small point: BRICSDecompose adds some CPU time and a fifth random forest adds about 25% to fit time. This should still fit well within the 10-minute limit.
Small point: a molecule that BRICS cannot split returns itself as one fragment. That is a legitimate feature, not a bug.
